### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal on a changed line), user.email (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via globalActions (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c5bef5f4ee5b3c5ed497e785b4d24f6b2649bf5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d29f84b404ce272c9443b5311c6f3d779214348c` — the merge of head `97432a19a480cfc368875eea2c923a01a3ab29c0` into base `6c5bef5f4ee5b3c5ed497e785b4d24f6b2649bf5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d29f84b404ce272c9443b5311c6f3d779214348c && git checkout d29f84b404ce272c9443b5311c6f3d779214348c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6c5bef5f4ee5b3c5ed497e785b4d24f6b2649bf5 97432a19a480cfc368875eea2c923a01a3ab29c0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6c5bef5f4ee5b3c5ed497e785b4d24f6b2649bf5 && git merge --no-ff 97432a19a480cfc368875eea2c923a01a3ab29c0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c5bef5f4ee5b3c5ed497e785b4d24f6b2649bf5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6c5bef5f4ee5b3c5ed497e785b4d24f6b2649bf5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `272a47c3b543b118623fc8029c8e69b9110fd06e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #21261 (body and all four comments: triage ruling (a) `5942994297`, claim `5945507055`, dev report `5946571239`, claim amendment `5946596296`), PR #21344 (body, 6-file list, net diff), the 35 check-runs on the head, and the repository at refs for the texts the diff cites. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head: 35, all `completed` — 32 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke: conditional jobs), 0 failure, 0 in progress.** `Type Check · debt ledger` is `success`, which answers the one family the dev left NOT MEASURED locally (`check:type-check-debt`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `TranslationDataSchema` — unchanged. Right.** No key is added, removed or retired; `globalActions` stays authorable for object-less actions, and `_actions` and `globalActions` are built by the one `actionTranslationSchema` factory (`translation.zod.ts:111`, `:353`, `:816`), which is why the helper's return type `NonNullable[TranslationData globalActions][string]` is sound for both branches. No tombstone, no `retiredKey()`, no `*_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE` entry is owed. `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness` are green; the dev's `check:api-surface` read "unchanged" is consistent with the diff.
2. **Public API of `@objectstack/spec` — unchanged. Right.** `actionTranslationNode` is module-private. `translateAction`, `resolveActionLabel`, `resolveActionConfirm`, `resolveActionSuccess`, `resolveActionResultDialog`, `translateObject`, `translateMetadataDocument` keep their signatures (`i18n-resolver.ts:606`, `:622`, `:666`, `:700`, `:1098`, `:1171`, `:2969` at head).
3. **Runtime behaviour — a bound action no longer reads `globalActions`. Right, and it is ruling (a).** At base `1371dc980c` the file carried exactly four `globalActions` code reads (`:563`, `:612`, `:716`, `:744`), matching the PR body's count; at head the only code read is inside the helper (`:585`), and all four lookups index off it. For an object-less action nothing changes: at base the object branch was skipped and the global key read; at head the global key is read. The resolver now agrees with the declaration (`translation.zod.ts:802-803`, "not bound to a specific object via `objectName`") and with the lint, which is the card's defect closed from the side triage chose.
4. **The key is the action's own `objectName`, never the caller's object — holds by construction. Right.** `translateAction` takes no caller object. `translateObject` scopes an inline action with `{ ...action, objectName }` before handing it to `translateAction` (head `:3031-:3045`), so an inline action is bound by declaration and never reaches `globalActions`. The objectui#3372 case (object-less action on an object's bar) has no spec-side counterpart, as the dev says; the object-less row is the spec's control. The triage's "objectui keys on the caller's object" concern is objectui's half, not reachable here.
5. **Lint — unchanged, and its message re-read true. Right.** `validate-translation-references.ts:1573-1578` at head: the action is "bound to object OWNER, so the resolver looks it up under `objects.OWNER._actions.X` — never under `globalActions`, which is only consulted for object-less actions. This key is never read." Every sentence is now true of the resolver; the hint ("Move these keys under `objects.OWNER._actions.X`") is the FROM → TO. Severity is still `TRANSLATION_TARGET_UNKNOWN_SEVERITY` (`:1357-1366`). The resolver's new header docblock claim that `os validate` names the object-scoped key to write is therefore true.
6. **No fifth reader. Right.** `git grep globalActions` over `packages/*/src` (non-test) at head: the CLI extractor is a producer and already files a bound action under `objects` (`cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts:1354`); `i18n-coverage.ts:190` merges bundles; the lint; a conversions key list (`conversions/registry.ts:7366`); the schema. No other resolver.
7. **Census — no in-repo move owed. Right.** `showcase_portfolio_snapshot` is object-less (`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts:436`, "NO objectName"), so its `globalActions` copy is correctly placed; no generated bundle under `**/translations/**` carries `globalActions`. So `pnpm check:i18n` is indeed not owed and no generated file is touched. The objectui preview-sample hit is objectui#11439's (see ③).
8. **Tests — the pins discriminate. Right.** The new describe block reads all four lookups off one `translateAction` result (`read()` → field, resultDialog, outcomeMessages, params) across six rows, each bundle parsed by `TranslationDataSchema`. The ablation reading (3 red: bound/global-only, inline/global-only, the replaced outcome row) is exactly the set that distinguishes fallback from no fallback; rows 2-5 pin behaviour that the mutation does not change, so they staying green under it is expected, not a gap. Fixture triage "replace" on `action-outcome-messages.test.ts` is right: the old row asserted the retired branch; the `globalActions` entry stays in the fixture as the negative. Test Core 1/6-6/6 green.
9. **Liveness ledger — text and anchor repoints only, no status change. Right.** `globalActions` row repointed to `#actionTranslationNode` with `verifiedAt` bumped to `2026-10-02` on a re-read; `objects` row's `_actions` anchor repointed with `verifiedAt` left at `2026-08-28` — right under the ledger README ("re-stamping the date without the reading is the downgrade"): only the `_actions` anchor was re-read, not the whole group. `action.json` `outcomeMessages` evidence reworded. `Spec property liveness` green.
10. **Docs — nothing owed in this diff. Right.** `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx:1053` already states the rule as ruled (PR #21304); the reference tables carry only shape text.
11. **Governed surfaces — none.** No path among the six is `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; the PR is neither Tier H nor Tier S, so this record is the dispatch's review of record, not a governed-landing credential. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21261-bound-action-global-fallback.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, body carrying `Clause-②: no` with no `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` arm; the PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no`. **Right, on all three counts.**

- `no` is right: ①.1 — the accept set is unchanged, the lint is unchanged, `TranslationDataSchema` parses the same inputs.
- Not BREAKING is right: nothing an author can write is removed or renamed; `globalActions` remains valid for object-less actions. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed, and triage ruled no conversion for a shape the door already refuses at error level. The dev's `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` reads are consistent; `Check Changeset` green.
- `patch` is right: a bug fix in a released package (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). The one observable change — a bound action with copy only under `globalActions` shows source text — is a runtime stopping to honour an input the contract's own door refuses at error level, which is the defect the card names, not a feature. The body states the FROM → TO one-liner and the runtime-stored-translation caveat anyway, which is more than `patch` requires.
- `skip-changeset` would be wrong: the resolver and the two `liveness/*.json` files ship in `@objectstack/spec`. Not applied — right.
- No model identifier in the changeset, the PR title or body.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `deviations`, each answered:

1. **Claim-surface breach (two `liveness/*.json` files)** — answered by the claim amendment `5946596296`; I read both hunks in the diff: text and an anchor repoint, no status change. Closed.
2. **`action-outcome-messages.test.ts` edited** — within the claim's "plus their tests"; the row pinned the retired branch. Closed.
3. **No pre-PR merge of `origin/main` (AGENTS.md §10)** — the head's merge-base with `origin/main` is `1371dc980c`; CI ran the merge ref against `222ecc27f9` (`mergeable_state: clean`, every check green). Since then `main` moved three commits to `04f0cc4992` (objectql, a skills doc, plugin-security), none touching `packages/spec`, `packages/lint`, the CLI extractor or any of the six files. No joint-breakage exposure measured; the queue's rebuilt generation is the second validation. Not a FAIL item. The seat does §10's scoped re-check only if `main` moves into `packages/spec` before landing.
4. **PR opened before the full suite finished** — the report carries every reading green and CI confirms. The PR body's "Still running…" bullet under "Verification at open" is now stale; the dev proposed the body edit and may not `PATCH` — **seat's optional edit**. Closed.
5. **Three gates exit 3 then 0 after prerequisite builds** — ordinary; CI owns them. Closed.
6. **`check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally** — `Type Check · debt ledger` success on this head. Closed.
7. **Commit trailers use the model-free pair** — that is AGENTS.md's own spelling, and AGENTS.md outranks the harness reminder. Closed.
8. **No spec counterpart to the objectui#3372 control** — verified by construction (①.4). Closed.

`open_questions`: none declared; nothing to answer.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, each escalated:

- **(a) objectui `apps/console/src/preview-samples.ts:492` (`globalActions.close_order`, bound to `sales_order`) and the `useObjectLabel-globalAction.test.tsx` docblock** — carrier objectstack-ai/objectui#11439, which triage made the seat's coordination child (`actionSuffixes` keyed on the action's own `objectName`, unlocked by the spec release carrying this PR). Not read here (outside this review's inputs). **Escalated to the seat:** confirm #11439 carries all three items (the `actionSuffixes` change, the sample move, the test docblock) and names this PR's release as its unlock. Note for that child: two spec docblocks describe objectui's reader as object-scoped-then-global (`action.zod.ts:956-958`, `translation.zod.ts:125-128`); they are true at today's pin and go stale when #11439 lands.
- **(b) The runtime publish door runs no `translation-target-unknown` on a translation write** (`validateTranslationReferences` declares no `runtimeTypes`, so it runs only on `flow` writes) — pre-existing, disclosed in the changeset body and the PR's Acceptance notes, "承接者:无". **Escalated to the seat:** the changeset now tells every project this hole exists, so either a card carries it (an authoring door open at runtime that `os validate` closes) or the seat rules it out of scope in writing.

Reviewer's own finding — one text the dev's census missed:

- **`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:1350-1351`** (the `outcomeMessages` property docblock) still reads: "**Translation** rides beside `successMessage`: `objects.OBJECT._actions.ACTION.outcomeMessages.OUTCOME`, **then** `globalActions.ACTION.outcomeMessages.OUTCOME` (`translateAction`)." The "then" states the retired order for `translateAction`, and `src/**/*.zod.ts` is in `@objectstack/spec`'s `files[]`, so this text ships — the same class the dev's rule-3 exception (text a release would freeze as wrong) made it fix the three ledger texts. No gate reads it; the `.describe()` customer string beside it is correct; the accept set and the resolver are unaffected, so it does not change the verdict on this head. **Escalated to the seat as owed text:** either fold the one-line rewording into this PR (a claim amendment for that docblock only, and a fresh record on the new head), or a docs-only follow-up PR before the release that carries this changeset.
